info.description:
# API Henrri Quickstart

Simplified guide for integrating Henrri invoicing services.

## 1. Authentification
`TTL: 600s` Refresh your token every 10 minutes.

> **POST** https://api-sandbox.henrri.io/v1/users/authenticate
```bash
curl -X POST https://api-sandbox.henrri.io/v1/users/authenticate \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "clientId": "YOUR_ID",
    "clientSecret": "YOUR_SECRET"
  }'
```
Success Response:

```bash
{
    "access_token": "eyJhbGci...",
    "expires_in": 600,
    "token_type": "Bearer",
    "refresh_token": "C5B217...",
    "scope": "Document_Read ..."
}
```

## 2. Connectivity Test (Hello World)
Use this endpoint to verify your credentials and token.

> **GET** https://api-sandbox.henrri.io/v1/secures/hello-world
```bash
curl -X GET https://api-sandbox.henrri.io/v1/secures/hello-world \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"
```

Expected Response:

```bash
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Test de connectivité réussi",
  "data": "Hello World"
}
```

## 3. Retrieve your User and Company information
Use this endpoint to get user and company information.

> **GET** https://api-sandbox.henrri.io/v1/users/me
```bash
curl -X GET https://api-sandbox.henrri.io/v1/users/me \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"
```

Success Response:

```bash
{
    "user": {
        "id": 11740,
        "email": "...",
        "firstName": "...",
        "lastName": "...",
        "urlImage": "...",
        ...
        "address": {
            "id": 10610,
            "address": "...",
            "city": "...",
            "postCode": "...",
            "country": "",
        }
    },
    "company": {
        "id": 1,
        "name": "...",
        "logoUrl": "...",
        ...
        "address": {
            "id": 2014,
            "address": "...",
            "city": "...",
            "postCode": "...",
            "country": "",
.        }
    }
}
```

| **Production** | https://api.henrri.io         |
| **Staging**    | https://api-sandbox.henrri.io |

get.summary: Get all the customers
get.description:
Get all customers with pagination, sorting and searching capabilities.

**Pagination:**
- `page`:page index requested. Starts at 1.
- `limit`:number of elements per pages query parameters. Default is 50, maximum is 100.

**Searching:**
- `search` : Search string to look for in customers

**Filtering:**
- `fromDate`/ `toDate`: Date range filtering on customers `creationDate`

**Sorting:**
- `sortBy`: Field to sort by
  - id:customer `id`
  - name:customer `name`
  - date:customer `creationDate`
- `sortOrder`: ascending or descending (default: desc)

**Response:**
- `elements` : list of customers for the current page
- `meta.page`:current page index (one-based)
- `meta.limit`:number of items per pages
- `meta.totalCount`:total number of items
- `meta.totalPages`:total number of pages
- `meta.hasNext`:indicates if a next page is available

Returns a paginated list of customers with their contacts.

🔒 **Requires Authorization (bearer token)**

🛡️ **Policies (Scopes) :** `Customer_Read`

post.description:
Create a new customer. The `contacts` field is required for all customer types.

**Validation rules:**
- The name, type and contacts fields are required
- Type must be 'professional' or 'individual'
- Professional customers must have between 1 and 4 contacts
- Individual customers must have exactly 1 contact
- Individual customers cannot have a SIRET/BCE number or corporate name extension
- Contact last name is required, email must be valid if provided
- If no primary contact is specified, the first contact will be marked as primary

**Company identifier (SIRET / BCE):**
- Use `companyIdentifierType` to specify the identifier format: `siret` or `bce`. Defaults to `siret` if omitted
- SIRET (France): must be exactly 14 digits
- BCE (Belgium): must be 10 digits starting with 0 or 1, with or without dots (e.g. 0123.456.789)

🔒 **Requires Authorization (bearer token)**

🛡️ **Policies (Scopes) :** `Customer_Write`

put.description:
Update an existing customer's information.

Replaces the customer data with the provided values.

**Address:**
The `address` field must be a structured object — passing a plain string will result in a 400 error.
```json
{ "address": "12 rue de la Paix", "city": "Paris", "postCode": "75001", "country": "France" }
```
If omitted, the existing address is preserved.

**Contacts:**
Contacts cannot be modified via this endpoint. Use `PUT /v1/customers/{id}/contacts/{contactId}` to update contacts.

**Company identifier (SIRET / BCE):**
- Use `companyIdentifierType` to specify the identifier format: `siret` or `bce`. Defaults to `siret` if omitted
- SIRET (France): must be exactly 14 digits
- BCE (Belgium): must be 10 digits starting with 0 or 1, with or without dots (e.g. 0123.456.789)

Modification is subject to business validation rules.
If an error occured, a detailed **BusinessError** object with a user-friendly message is returned. Business errors can be found in section Business Errors > Customer retrieval and manipulation.


🔒 **Requires Authorization (bearer token)**

🛡️ **Policies (Scopes) :** `Customer_Write`

Create a document line.
Required fields:
- `typeId` : type of line ; can be recovered with GET on /documentlinetypes

Two line creation scenario are possible.

### Billable item line

If you wish to create a line representing a billable item, you must provide:
- `typeId`
- `itemId` or an `item` object:referencing a billable item

### Text line

If you wish to add a text line, you must provide:
- `typeId`
- `description` : the text

For text lines, you can also provide an `itemId` referencing an existing text item (see `/v1/textitems`).

### Layout line

If you wish to add a layout line (horizontalLine, lineBreak, total, subTotal), you must provide:
- `typeId`

### Tax entry mode

A document is entirely entered with tax included, or entirely without tax — never a mix.
`isTaxIncluded` on a billable item line must match the document it belongs to, or the request is rejected.

get.summary: Generate a document pdf
get.description:
Returns the document rendered as a PDF file (`application/pdf`), named after the document.

A finalized document is always rendered the way it was locked. A draft is rendered from its current
content, so the file changes as long as the document is edited.

**Factur-X (electronic invoicing):** set `isFacturX=true` to get a hybrid PDF — the same readable
document, with the structured invoice data embedded inside the file as a `factur-x.xml` attachment.
The XML follows the Factur-X / ZUGFeRD **EN 16931** profile, which is the format expected by your
customer's invoicing platform.

> Ask for Factur-X on invoices only: the structured data describes an invoice, so generating it for a
> quotation or a delivery note produces a file no platform will accept. The customer address, the SIRET
> or VAT number and the VAT rates must be filled in on the document, otherwise the embedded data is
> incomplete. The PDF itself is identical with or without the option.

If the rendering service is saturated, a `503` is returned with a `Retry-After` header: retry in a few
seconds. Prefer `POST /documents/{id}/pdf/url` when you want a link to download the file later
(Factur-X is not available on that route).

🔒 **Requires Authorization (bearer token)**

🛡️ **Policies (Scopes) :** `Document_Read`

post.summary: Transform a finalized quote into a draft invoice
post.description:
Creates an invoice from a finalized quotation.
`{id}` is the id of the quotation; the response is the **new invoice**, with its own id.

**What is carried over**

- the customer of the quotation
- every line, in the same order, with the same quantities, prices, VAT rates and discounts
- the title, the subtitle and the price-entry mode (excl./incl. tax)
- the payment milestones of the quotation, recreated on the invoice with due dates recomputed
  from the invoice date and the payment terms

The invoice is dated the day of the call and is created as a **draft**: it has no final number yet,
so you can still edit it.
Call `POST /documents/{id}/finalize` to lock it and get its final number.

**Rules**

- the source document must be a quotation, and it must be finalized
- a quotation can be invoiced only once; if it was already turned into an invoice or into a delivery
  note, the call is refused (invoice the delivery note instead)
- once transformed, the quotation is marked as invoiced in Henrri

**Responses**

`201 Created` with the new invoice, and a `Location` header pointing to `GET /documents/{newId}`.
Refusals come back as a **BusinessError** object with one of the codes listed in
*Business Errors > Document transformation*.

quantity.description: Quantity of the line item, representing the number of units or amount of the product or service being invoiced. This value is used in conjunction with the selling price and VAT rate to calculate the total price and tax amount for the line item. The quantity can be a decimal value to accommodate cases where partial units are allowed (e.g., weight-based products or services billed by time).

isTaxIncluded.description:
Indicates whether the selling price of the line item includes tax. This property is used to determine how the total price and tax amount for the line item should be calculated. When IsTaxIncluded is set to true, it signifies that the selling price already includes tax, and the tax amount can be derived from the total price. Conversely, when IsTaxIncluded is set to false, it indicates that the selling price does not include tax, and the tax amount should be calculated separately based on the VAT rate and added to the total price of the line item.
**Optional.** When omitted, it defaults to the tax entry mode of the document. A document is entirely
entered with tax included or entirely without tax, never a mix — a line with a different, explicitly set
value is rejected with a business error.

totalWithoutTax.description: Total price of the line item without tax. This value is calculated based on the selling price, quantity, and VAT rate, and it represents the total amount for the line item before any taxes are applied. The TotalWithoutTax can be used for internal calculations, reporting, and displaying the base price of the line item in the document.

totalWithTax.description: Total price of the line item with tax. This value is calculated based on the selling price, quantity, and VAT rate, and it represents the total amount for the line item after taxes are applied. The TotalWithTax can be used for displaying the final price of the line item in the document, including the tax amount, and for financial reporting purposes to reflect the total cost to the customer.

areElementsOfGroupShown.description: Indicates whether the elements of the group to which this line belongs are shown in the document. This property is used to determine if the line item is part of a group and whether the details of that group should be displayed in the document. When AreElementsOfGroupShown is set to true, it signifies that the line item is associated with a group and that the individual line items within that group should be visible in the document, allowing for a more detailed presentation of related line items together.

lineNumber.description: One-based index of the line in the document.

isAGroup.description: Whether the line item is a group header, indicating that it serves as a parent line for a group of related line items. This property is used to identify lines that act as group headers, allowing for the organization and grouping of related line items together. When IsAGroup is set to true, it indicates that the line item is a group header, and the GroupId property can be used to specify which lines belong to this group. This association can be useful for calculating totals, applying discounts, or displaying related line items together in the document.

doesGroupOwnDifferentVat.description: Whether the line item has a different VAT rate than the other lines in the same group. isMemberOfAGroup.description: Whether the line is a member of a group, indicating that it belongs to a specific group of lines within the document. This association can be useful for calculating totals, applying discounts, or displaying related line items together in the document.

isAdjustmentOfGroup.description: Whether the line is an adjustment of a group, meaning it is used to adjust the total of a group of lines. This property indicates that the line serves as a correction or modification to the overall total of a group, allowing for adjustments to be made without altering the individual line items within the group. An adjustment line can be used to apply discounts, surcharges, or other modifications to the total amount of a group of lines while keeping the original line items intact.

# API Credits & Quotas

The Henrri API (only in production) uses a **monthly credit** model. Each API plan comes with a monthly
allowance of credits; only a few high-value actions consume credits, and everything
else is free.

> The authoritative cost of an endpoint is shown as a **badge** directly on that endpoint
> in this reference. The tables below reflect the current configuration.

## What costs credits

Credits are charged only when a commercial document is **issued** (finalized) or when a
quote is **validated**. Building documents up to that point is free.

| Action | Endpoint | Cost |
| :-- | :-- | :-: |
| Finalize an **accounting** document (invoice, credit note) | `POST /documents/{id}/finalize` | **8** |
| Finalize a non-accounting document (quote, etc.) | `POST /documents/{id}/finalize` | **2** |
| Validate a quote (accepted / signed) | `POST /documents/{id}/validate` | **2** |

The cost of finalizing depends on the document type: an **accounting** document
(`documentType.isAccounting = true`, i.e. invoices and credit notes) costs more than a
non-accounting one. All other create/update/delete operations, and **all read
operations**, are free.

## What is free

- All **read** operations (`GET`), including listing, PDF/export retrieval, statistics.
- Building and editing a document before issuing it: creating/updating the document,
  **adding, editing, moving or deleting lines**, managing customers, items, categories, etc.
- Authentication and token refresh.
- Any write that fails: a request returning an error (HTTP `>= 400`) is **not** charged.

## Monthly quotas

Each API plan has a monthly credit allowance. The quota resets on the 1st of each
calendar month (UTC).

| Plan | Monthly credits |
| :-- | :-: |
| API 1 | 200 |
| API 2 | 1 000 |
| API 3 | 2 000 |
| API 4 | 4 000 |

Because only issuance consumes credits, the allowance maps directly to a number of issued
documents per month. The exact count depends on your mix of accounting documents (8
credits) and quotes/validations (2 credits) — e.g. an *API 1* plan covers up to 100
validated quotes, or about 25 invoices, per month.

## Monitoring your consumption

Every authenticated response includes credit headers so you can track usage in real time
without a dedicated call:

| Header | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- |
| `X-Credits-Used` | Credits consumed during the current calendar month. |
| `X-Credits-Limit` | Your plan's monthly quota (`unlimited` for uncapped clients). |
| `X-Credits-Remaining` | Credits left for the current month (`unlimited` when uncapped). |

## When the quota is reached

Once the monthly quota is exhausted, chargeable actions return **HTTP 429 Too Many
Requests** with a JSON body:

```json
{
  "code": "QUOTA_EXCEEDED",
  "message": "You have exceeded your monthly Quota of 200 API calls.",
  "current_usage": 201
}
```

Read operations keep working — only credit-consuming actions are blocked. The quota
becomes available again at the start of the next month.

> Note: `429` is also returned by the per-minute **rate limiter** (a different limit). Rate
> limiting is reported through the `X-RateLimit-*` headers; the credit quota is reported
> through the `X-Credits-*` headers above.

All notable, consumer-facing changes to the Henrri API are documented here, grouped by month (most recent first).
August 2026 ### Added - **Users**: full CRUD (list, get, create, update, delete); responses now include the user role. - **Webhooks**: test ping endpoint; failed or undelivered events are retried automatically. - **IP restriction**: calls can be limited to a list of allowed IP addresses. - Payment-terms display: read and customise the payment-terms label of a document. - Authentication from the reference with your client key and secret, or your Henrri login / password. ### Changed - Business error messages reviewed. - Lists return an empty array instead of `null`. - `410` is no longer part of the documented responses, `404` are used instead. - Documentation enhanced. ### Fixed - Accuracy of consumed-credits reporting (values returned in the `X-Credits-*` headers). - Item deletion no longer fails in some scenarios. - Default payment terms not applied to a document created through the API. - Document lines losing their company link after an update. - Retrieving a document that does not exist. - Webhooks: delivery id was shared between subscriptions. - `GET /users/{id}/address` now applies the same access checks as `GET /users/{id}`.
July 2026 ### Fixed - Accuracy of consumed-credits reporting (values returned in the `X-Credits-*` headers). - Item deletion no longer fails in some scenarios. ### Changed - Documentation: sections reordered; the **Credits** guide (quotas, consumption rules) is now part of this documentation.
June 2026 ### Added - `X-Credits-*` response headers on every call, reporting credit consumption and remaining quota. Credit info also includes your subscription option. - **Text items**: items of type *text* (line comments) with dedicated endpoints, query parameters and specific business errors. - Payment indication on documents: responses now tell whether a document is paid. - HATEOAS links for customer contacts and bank resources. ### Changed - Default rate limit raised to **100 calls per hour**. - Webhooks: create/update now accepts several event types in one call; creating an existing webhook updates it. - API version is no longer read from the `Accept` header. - Documentation: full review of endpoint, model and response descriptions; note that the OpenAPI document is AI-friendly. ### Fixed - Retrieving the detail of a document that has no lines. - Search now handles emojis and extended Unicode characters.
May 2026 ### Added - **Payments & payment milestones**: list milestones of a document or customer, pay one or several milestones, retrieve the payment linked to a milestone, list payment modes, filter payments by state, filter and sort the payments list (paginated). - PDF: `POST /pdf/url` and `GET /pdf/files/{guid}` to generate then download a PDF. - `Retry-After` and `X-RateLimit-*` headers on `429` responses (and rate-limit headers on all responses). ### Changed - All `400` errors now use the RFC 7807 `ProblemDetails` format. - `vatRate` renamed to `vatPercent`; accepts a flexible range instead of a fixed list. - Pagination: `limit` clamped between 1 and 100 (default 50); invalid values return `400`. - Documents: default sort order defined; sorting by bank available. - `contacts` is no longer required when creating a customer; `dueDate` is nullable; `sellingPriceWithoutTax` and the VAT rate are nullable on document lines. - Default dates applied when `fromDate` / `toDate` are omitted. ### Fixed - **Security hardening**: every resource you read, modify or delete is now strictly checked against the company of your token (customers, contacts, documents, items, units, payments, banks…). Text fields are sanitized. - The `finalized` field can no longer be modified through document edition. - `503` returned when the PDF generator is saturated (instead of a hang); PDF generation stability improved. - Item references (`parentItemId`, `itemCategoryId`, `unitId`) are validated against your company.
April 2026 ### Added - **Webhooks**: manage webhooks through the API-keys endpoints, HMAC secret generation, event delivery (document, customer, item events…). - Endpoint to **transform a quote into an invoice**. - Document milestones endpoint. ### Changed - `GET /documentTypes` returns a plain (non-paginated) list. - Business errors are documented individually instead of one large table. - `best-sales` route renamed. ### Fixed - `500` errors on empty POST bodies and on sorting by a non-existent field. - A finalized document can no longer be updated. - Customer soft delete. - Authentication response documentation.
March 2026 ### Added - **Detailed error responses**: `404` and `500` now carry a title and a detailed message; business errors returned as structured problems; dedicated error-documentation page linked from endpoints. - Field validation wave: VAT rate/percent, required `customerId` on documents, bank fields, postal codes, SIRET/BCE, phone numbers, emails. - Required scopes, deprecation notices and anonymous endpoints are now generated automatically in the documentation. - Credit limits per API plan and API-call metering. ### Changed - Creating a document line returns the fully computed line. - Lines cannot be created inside `POST /documents` (use the document-lines endpoints). - A line requires a `designation` or a `reference`. - Disabled API keys are no longer returned. ### Fixed - Customer address missing from GET/POST/PUT responses. - Customer search by city / postal code. - Removed duplicate `descriptionWithHtml` field.
February 2026 ### Added - `GET /itemCategories`, `GET /documentTypes`, `GET /users/me`. - **Document finalization** endpoint with translated validation problems and alerts. - Document lines: paginated list, move and delete. - SIRET / BCE company identifier support (`companyIdentifierType`). - Company address included in `GET /companies/{id}`. - Postman collection covering all endpoints. ### Changed - **Response format overhaul**: list metadata moved to a `meta` sub-object; all properties in camelCase; POST endpoints switched from form-encoded to JSON. - `authenticate` accepts both JSON and form input. - `GeneratePdf` renamed to `GetPdf`. - `size` parameter replaced by `limit`. - Removed `deliveryAddress` from Customer and `email` / `phoneNumber` from Address. ### Fixed - Filtering between two dates.
January 2026 — API v1.0 ### Added - **Customers & contacts**: full CRUD. - **Documents**: create, update, delete. - **Document lines**: create, read, update, delete, with item (article) relation. - **Items**: add, modify (delete arrived in February); item categories and families. - **Units** endpoints. - Introduction page in this documentation; dev API keys and bearer-token testing in the reference. ### Changed - Consistent naming: camelCase JSON everywhere, `tradeName`, `service` / `product` item kinds, cleaned-up enums (unused values removed). - Validation logic moved to the business layer; contacts reloaded after customer creation.
2025 and earlier — foundations (pre-release) - Authentication server, API keys and JWT bearer authentication. - Redis hybrid cache, native rate limiter, structured logging (Serilog + OpenTelemetry). - Analytics endpoints: monthly / yearly revenues, best sales by item and by customer. - Quote-sharing extranet: PDF generation, quote validation and follow-up.

Subscribable webhooks triggered when events occur in Henrri.

## Setup

Log in to Henrri, add a callback URL, then select the events you want to subscribe to and save.

> Your callback must answer with any `2XX` status code for a delivery to be considered received.

Before subscribing, use the test button: it pings your callback with the same payload envelope
and signature headers as a real event.

```json
{
  "event": "webhook.test",
  "date": "2026-08-04T10:05:46.9544195+00:00",
  "id": 0,
  "companyId": 1,
  "delivery": "9ae2c66b-2c51-409a-8eab-e130d67cbcc1"
}
```

In a test ping, `event` is always `webhook.test` and `id` always `0` — no business resource is
involved. `companyId` is your company identifier, `date` the time of the ping, and `delivery` a
new identifier generated for every send.

> A failed test is never retried: fix your callback, then press the button again.

## Lifecycle

Events are raised by your actions in Henrri as well as by write operations on this API.

The delivery is sent once, as soon as the event occurs.

> **No automatic retry yet.** If your callback does not answer `2XX`, or cannot be reached, the
> delivery is marked as failed and is **not** sent again. Automatic retries are being worked on.

> The delivery history is available in Henrri, on the same tab where you configured your
> subscriptions. A failed delivery shows the status code or the error returned by your callback.

Headers: `X-Henrri-Webhook-Signature` (`sha256=<hex>`), `X-Henrri-Webhook-Delivery` (delivery GUID), `X-Henrri-Webhook-Timestamp` (unix seconds). Verify with `HMAC-SHA256(secret, "{timestamp}.{rawBody}")`, hex lowercase. Acknowledge by returning any 2xx status.
